newsitem.title: RUSSIA: India not seeking Russian military pact - minister.
newsitem.headline: India not seeking Russian military pact - minister.

text.p: India's external affairs minister said on Wednesday New Delhi would continue buying Moscow's military hardware, but did not want any military ties.
"India, neither in the past, nor now, nor for the future, thinks in terms of military alliances against anybody," I.K. Gujral said at the end of a visit to Moscow.
"Russia has not sought at any stage any military alliance with India, nor has India asked Russia."
Russia is currently fighting a war of words with the West about plans to invite new members from eastern Europe into NATO.
Maverick ultranationalist lawmaker Vladimir Zhironovsky, in remarks quoted by Interfax news agency, recently called for an alliance between Russia, India and other nations to counterbalance NATO.
Gujral said he had discussed India's interest in buying Russian arms in four days of talks with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and other Russian officials, but gave no details.

Russia, and the Soviet Union before it, is India's main supplier of weapons. Moscow is due to deliver the first eight of 40 Su-30MK fighter jets ordered by the Indian Air Force next month. The deal, signed last year, is worth $1.8 billion.
Gujral said India also planned to go ahead with the purchase of two Russian light water nuclear reactors, despite reported objections from the United States.
"I am not aware of any such objections," he told reporters. "These agreements have been in force and remain in force."

The United States, worried that India is not a signatory to the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and could use the technology for military purposes, has urged Russia to drop the $2.6 billion sale, agreed in 1988.
But Russian officials reiterated this week they would go ahead with the agreement.

Gujral, a former ambassador to Moscow, said the two countries had discussed a planned summit between Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, but said only that both sides were keen to meet soon.
